knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.8
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes the bootstrap method for obtaining a confidence interval?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Bootstrap CIs use the replicate distribution of the statistic to form endpoints. Estimating an SE alone is not yet an interval method of the same kind, and hypothesis testing is a different task.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Resample, recompute the statistic, form endpoints from the bootstrap distribution (e.g. percentiles).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Equating bootstrap SE estimation or hypothesis testing with bootstrap CI construction.

choices.label: Resample from the sample, recompute the statistic on each replicate, and form interval endpoints from that bootstrap distribution (for example a percentile interval).
Estimate only the standard error of an estimator by bootstrap; that SE estimate is already a confidence interval.
Bootstrap confidence intervals are the same procedure as a hypothesis test: both decide whether to reject a null.
A bootstrap CI is formed by taking the Normal-mean cookbook interval and replacing s with a single bootstrap draw.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.8
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly outlines a percentile bootstrap confidence interval and keeps related ideas distinct?
knowledge_checks.body: Percentile bootstrap CI; refuse SE-only and HT conflation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Percentile intervals use replicate quantiles. SE-only summaries and hypothesis-test decisions are different objects.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Percentile endpoints from bootstrap replicates; distinct from SE-only bootstrap and from HT.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating bootstrap SE estimation or a reject/retain decision as the bootstrap CI.

choices.label: Resample with replacement, recompute the statistic on each resample, then take the α/2 and 1−α/2 quantiles of those replicates as interval endpoints. Estimating a bootstrap standard error alone is not the same as constructing that CI, and forming the CI is not a hypothesis test.
Compute a bootstrap SE and report (θ̂ − SE, θ̂ + SE) only; quantile endpoints from replicates are never used.
A bootstrap CI is completed by rejecting H₀ whenever θ̂ falls outside a fixed null value, without forming interval endpoints.
Draw one bootstrap resample, compute θ̂*, and report the singleton interval [θ̂*, θ̂*].
